correctness.rationale: The affine-coordinate adjoint identity is reconstructed explicitly, including both drift divergence and neutral second divergence. All boundary-normal coefficients vanish. A constant-density weak killed-forward solution is unique by well-posedness of the stopped Wright–Fisher problem. For positive selection, constant adjoint value forces balance via the skew matrix and simplex barycenter. The positive product is a right eigenfunction, and its Doob drift gives a Dirichlet(2) invariant probability. The exact checker corroborates algebra but finite data is not used as infinite proof.

value.rationale: First-extinction and conditional coexistence are natural multitype population stochastic observables. The theorem completely classifies selection-preserving uniform quasi-stationarity under tournament interactions, identifies exact exponential survival independent of arbitrary positive selection, and yields an explicit invariant law for the conditioned diffusion. This is beyond a routine finite computation or a generic generator renaming.
